steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Film genre is a categorisation system that groups films sharing similar narrative patterns, visual styles, themes and emotional effects.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Steve Neale argued that genre depends on both repetition of conventions and difference and variation to sustain audience interest.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The 'repertoire of elements' describes the set of conventions that characterise a genre — setting, character types, iconography, narratives and themes.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Iconography refers to the visual symbols and recurring images associated with a genre: cowboy hats in westerns, spaceships in sci-fi, masks in horror.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What did Steve Neale mean by saying genre requires both repetition and difference? | Q: Explain the difference between Altman's semantic and syntactic approaches to genre. | Q: How do genre conventions serve both the film industry and the audience?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Neale argued that genre depends on a balance between the familiar and the new. Pure repetition would make every genre film identical and boring; pure difference would make it unrecognisable as genre.  | Altman's semantic approach identifies the surface elements of a genre — its iconography, settings, character types and visual motifs. For Westerns, semantic elements include cowboys, horses, saloons a | For the industry, genre conventions provide a production framework that reduces financial risk by targeting proven audience preferences. Marketing relies on genre to communicate what a film offers. Fo

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Name specific theorists — Neale, Altman — and use their terminology accurately. Always illustrate genre theory with concrete film examples — never discuss genre in the abstract. Show how a film both follows and deviates from genre conventions — most interesting films do both. Consider the genre cycle position of your set films: are they classic, revisionist or parodic examples? Link genre to audience: explain why conventions matter to viewers, not just to filmmakers and studios.
